channel.title: Poland Closer — Blog
channel.description: Slow travel articles, guides, and inspiration for Poland.

item.title: Weekend in Zakopane — A 3-Day Plan
item.description: Zakopane is the winter capital of Poland and the gateway to the Tatras. Here is a 3-day plan to see the most important places and feel the atmosphere of Podhale.

item.title: Weekend in Roztocze — A 3-Day Plan
item.description: Roztocze is a land of gentle hills, loess ravines, and pine forests. Here is a 3-day plan to see the most beautiful corners of the region.

item.title: Weekend in the Tricity — A 3-Day Plan
item.description: Gdańsk, Sopot, and Gdynia are three cities that form one of the most interesting places in Poland. Here is a 3-day plan to see the most important places in the Tricity.

item.title: Weekend in Kraków — A 2-Day Plan
item.description: Kraków is one of the most beautiful cities in Poland — full of history, culture, and flavors. Here is a 2-day plan to see the most important places and feel the atmosphere of the city.

item.title: Weekend in Masuria — A 3-Day Plan
item.description: Masuria is the land of a thousand lakes — perfect for a slow weekend. Here is a 3-day plan to see the most beautiful corners of the region.

item.title: Weekend in the Karkonosze — A 3-Day Plan
item.description: The Karkonosze are the most dramatic mountains in Poland — raw, windy, and full of contrasts. Here is a 3-day plan to see the most beautiful corners of the region.

item.title: West Pomeranian Cuisine — Fish, Paprykarz, and Herring
item.description: West Pomeranian cuisine is the taste of the Baltic and the Szczecin Lagoon. Find out what is worth eating in Szczecin and on the western coast.

item.title: Kuyavian Cuisine — Toruń Gingerbread, Żur, and Kołocz
item.description: Kuyavian-Pomeranian cuisine is a mix of agricultural and burgher traditions. Find out what is worth eating in Toruń and Kuyavia.

item.title: Masovian Cuisine — Flaki, Krupnik, and Liver
item.description: Masovian cuisine is a mix of rural and Warsaw traditions. Find out what is worth eating in Warsaw and Masovia.

item.title: Subcarpathian Cuisine — Proziaki, Fuczki, and Hreczanyki
item.description: Subcarpathian cuisine is a mix of Polish, Ukrainian, and Lemko traditions. Find out what is worth eating in the Bieszczady and Subcarpathia.

item.title: Lower Silesian Cuisine — Silesian Heaven, Duck, and Dumplings
item.description: Lower Silesian cuisine is a mix of Polish, German, and Czech traditions. Find out what is worth eating in Wrocław and Lower Silesia.

item.title: Pomeranian Cuisine — Fish, Herring, and Golce
item.description: Pomeranian cuisine is the taste of the Baltic meeting Hanseatic tradition. Find out what is worth eating on the coast — from herring to golce.

item.title: Lesser Poland Cuisine — Obwarzanek, Żurek, and Makowiec
item.description: Lesser Poland cuisine is a mix of Kraków, Podhale, and rural traditions. Find out what is worth eating in a region where East and West meet.

item.title: Warmia-Masuria Cuisine — Vendace, Marzipan, and Kindziuk
item.description: The cuisine of Warmia and Masuria is fish from the lakes, game, mushrooms, and Olsztyn marzipan. Find out what is worth eating in the land of a thousand lakes.

item.title: Greater Poland Cuisine — Croissants, Pyry, and Goose
item.description: Greater Poland cuisine is potatoes in every form, croissants with white poppy seeds, and goose for St. Martin's Day. Find out what is worth eating in the region.

item.title: Lublin Cuisine — Cebularze, Pierogi with Bryndza, and Roztocze Trout
item.description: The cuisine of the Lublin region is a mix of Polish, Ukrainian, and Jewish traditions. Find out what is worth eating in a region where East and West meet.

item.title: Kashubian Cuisine — Herring, Eel, and Kashubian Broth
item.description: Kashubian cuisine is the taste of the sea meeting the forest. Find out what is worth eating in Kashubia — from herring to smoked eel.

item.title: Silesian Cuisine — Roulade, Dumplings, and Modra Kapusta
item.description: Silesian cuisine is substance, heartiness, and respect for tradition. Find out what is worth eating in Silesia — from roulade to kołocz.

item.title: Podhale Cuisine — Oscypek, Kwaśnica, and Bryjka
item.description: Podhale cuisine is the cuisine of shepherds — thick, hearty, based on milk, cheese, cabbage, and potatoes. Find out what is worth trying in the mountains.

item.title: Podlasie Cuisine — Kibiny, Kartacze, and Potato Babka
item.description: Podlasie cuisine is a mix of Polish, Tatar, Orthodox, and Jewish traditions. Find out what is worth eating in a region where cultures cross.

item.title: By Bike Around Poland — How to Plan Your First Multi-Day Trip
item.description: Green Velo, Velo Dunajec, Velo Baltica — Poland has more and more cycling routes. Find out how to plan your first multi-day cycling trip.

item.title: Poland in Spring — 7 Places That Wake Up to Life
item.description: Spring is the best time to travel around Poland. Birds return, trees bloom, and the crowds haven't arrived yet. Here are 7 places that particularly delight in spring.

item.title: How to Plan a Slow Weekend Trip
item.description: A weekend is only 48 hours. But properly planned, it can give more than a week in a hurry. Here are 7 rules for planning a slow weekend.

item.title: Silesian Castle Trail — 5 Strongholds in One Weekend
item.description: Silesia is the most castle-rich region in Poland. From Ogrodzieniec to Pszczyna — here are 5 strongholds worth seeing in one weekend.

item.title: Masuria Without Sails — 5 Ideas for Non-Sailors
item.description: Masuria is not just sails and yachts. Find out what you can do in Masuria if you don't like sailing — and still want to feel the atmosphere of the region.

item.title: What to Eat in Kraków — 10 Dishes You Must Try
item.description: Kraków is not just obwarzanek and pierogi. Find out what is truly worth eating in the capital of Lesser Poland — from obwarzanek to the Okrąglak zapiekanka.

item.title: Podlasie — A Weekend with Bison and Orthodox Churches
item.description: A weekend plan for the wildest region of Poland. Białowieża, Biebrza, Supraśl — three days in a land of forests and multiculturalism.

item.title: Winter in the Tatras — Why It's the Best Season
item.description: Zakopane can be crowded in winter, but the Tatras in winter are quiet, white, and completely different from summer. Here are 5 reasons to come here in winter.

item.title: Poland in Autumn — 7 Places That Look Like a Fairytale
item.description: Polish autumn is golden leaves, mists over lakes, and empty trails. Here are 7 places that particularly delight at this time of year.

item.title: How to Travel in Poland Without a Car
item.description: Train, bus, bike — Poland is much better connected than it seems. A guide to traveling without a car.

item.title: Polish Regional Cuisine — 10 Dishes You Must Try
item.description: Kibiny, oscypek, kartacze, roulade — Polish cuisine is not just pierogi and pork chops. It is a dozen different regional cuisines, each with its own history.

item.title: When to Visit the Baltic to Avoid the Crowds
item.description: July and August are peak season. But the Baltic has other faces too — quieter, cheaper, and often more beautiful.

item.title: Weekend in the Bieszczady — A 3-Day Plan
item.description: Three days is the minimum to truly feel the Bieszczady. A plan that lets you see the mountain meadows, Orthodox churches, and the lake — without haste.

item.title: Slow Travel — What Does It Actually Mean?
item.description: Slow travel is not just another trend. It is a way of thinking about travel in which the quality of the experience matters more than the number of places ticked off.
